name: task-control-architecture
context: Framework for building task-level control systems in autonomous robots and agents, providing hierarchical task decomposition, temporal constraint management, and implicit invocation communication
benefits: Hierarchical task decomposition for complex goal breakdown
Implicit invocation for decoupled task producers and consumers
Concurrent execution with temporal constraint management
Fault tolerance via redundant multiple handlers
Execution monitoring with automated condition watching
Human-in-the-loop interaction at any hierarchy level
Cross-language support (Lisp and C via TCP/IP)
tradeoffs: Central server bottleneck limits horizontal scalability
Complexity requires understanding of task trees, temporal constraints, monitors, exception handlers
Single point of failure in central server
Not appropriate for hard real-time control systems
Task tree coordination adds network latency across processes
use_cases: NASA rovers: Ambler, Ratler, Nomad for planetary exploration
Dante robot: Volcanic exploration with autonomous navigation
Autonomous spacecraft simulation with mission-level control
Xavier mobile robot: Indoor navigation with complex task hierarchies
avoid_when: Simple CRUD operations without complex coordination needs
Centralized architecture is prohibited by policy
Team lacks experience with hierarchical task management
Project needs simple lightweight task sequencing
component_types: Task Decomposition: Hierarchical decomposition of goals into subtasks with temporal constraints
Scheduler: Executes planned behaviors based on temporal constraints; manages execution order
Monitor: Watches selected sensors and triggers actions when conditions are met
Resource Manager: Orderly access to shared resources; handles queuing of resource requests
Exception Handler: Context-dependent error procedures: terminate, suspend, patch, or retry plans
Message Server: Central hub for publish/subscribe and client/server communication
Human Interface: Interactive task monitoring and modification at any hierarchy level
technology_stack: Languages: Lisp, C (cross-language TCP/IP socket communication)
Evolution: TCA -> TCM (C++ library) -> TDL (C++ superset) -> IPC
Message passing: TCP/IP sockets with automatic marshalling/unmarshalling
Robot applications: ControlShell integration for real-time control
anti_patterns: Sequential sense-plan-act (failing to exploit concurrent execution)
Tight coupling (direct module-to-module communication bypassing implicit invocation)
Single handler per signal (not utilizing fault tolerance through redundant handlers)
Ignoring temporal constraints (over-sequential execution prevents parallel optimization)
design_principles: Hierarchical Task Design: Break complex goals into clear subtask hierarchies with well-defined temporal constraints
Redundant Handler Registration: Register multiple handlers for critical signals to ensure fault tolerance
Monitor Placement: Place monitors strategically to watch key sensors and conditions for early fault detection
Temporal Constraint Optimization: Leverage concurrent execution opportunities by analyzing temporal constraints
Resource Queuing: Use Resource Manager for orderly access to prevent conflicts in shared resources
Checkpoint Progress: Save execution state periodically for recovery from failures
Cross-Language Communication: Use TCP/IP socket communication for Lisp and C process integration
Human Intervention Points: Designate checkpoints for human oversight and approval in critical workflows
best_practices: Start With a Shallow Hierarchy: Model top-level tasks first and decompose only where temporal constraints genuinely require concurrency
Register Redundant Handlers for Critical Signals: Attach at least two handlers to failure-sensitive signals so a single handler crash cannot stall the mission
Tune Monitor Polling Intervals: Balance early fault detection against CPU/network overhead; avoid polling sensors faster than they update
Test Exception Paths Explicitly: Simulate handler crashes, resource contention, and deadline misses to verify terminate/suspend/patch/retry behavior
Version Task Trees Alongside Code: Keep task decomposition definitions in version control so mission profiles are reproducible
Instrument Task Execution Times: Log planned vs actual durations per subtask to refine temporal constraints over successive runs
Isolate Real-Time Control From Task Control: Run hard real-time loops (e.g., servo control) on dedicated controllers; reserve TCA/TCM/TDL for task-level coordination
